column1: # PLeaTTa Perf-1 Phase A0: measured dominant-cost classification.
# Raw, reproducible rows are in perf-a0.tsv and perf-a0-scan.tsv; each row
# records the exact generated source hash, wall time, machine steps, peak
# substitution size, world sizes, and candidate-scan counter.
#   case                 n=100   n=200   n=400   steps@400  maxSubst@400
# Ordinary self-space add is O(1) (`a :: selfAtoms`) and adds little over the
# constant-space control.  The shared superlinearity is resolution/substitution
# maintenance: machine steps are linear while the active substitution grows
# one binding per recursive frame.  Exact dedup adds a real scan cost on top.
# Hence ordered indices are useful for selective space queries, exact dedup,
# and large live clause databases, but they are not the first root fix for the
# 18 families.  Open enumeration must still visit every answer.
# Post-index result: ordered clause and space indices are now integrated and
# proved.  Selective bound-head query overhead at n=4000 fell from about
# .034s to .015s after subtracting source loading, and exact-dedup n=400 fell
# from 1.172s to 1.012s.  peano, peanofast, and tilepuzzle nevertheless still
# time out at 30s; their dominant remaining work is substitution/term growth
# or total BFS reductions, not candidate discovery.
#   INDEX-DELIVERED    indexing measurably improves a real subpath but the
#                      full family remains bound by a named different cost
#   SECONDARY         indexing helps a subpath but cannot close the family
#   NOT-INDEX         dominant cost needs another mechanism
